newsitem.title: JAPAN: Continuing Japan income tax cuts may be hard - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Continuing Japan income tax cuts may be hard - MOF.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday that some in Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) held the view that it may be difficult to extend special income tax cuts into the next fiscal year.

Asked how LDP members reacted to Mitsuzuka's comments on Tuesday that continuing special income tax cuts would be difficult, Mitsuzuka said: "Concerning this issue, there are some within the party who said they personally agreed with what the finance minister was saying."
But he added that further discussion was needed in settings such as a parliament committee to be formed to discuss taxes, and that economic conditions should also be taken into account.
The Japanese government has implemented special income tax cuts, worth two trillion yen annually, for three consecutive years as a way to boost the economy.
Concerning Japan's corporate taxes, which are among the highest in world, Mitsuzuka said lowering corporate taxes while expanding the tax base was one option to be considered.
A senior LDP official has been reported as saying that corporate taxes should be cut by five percent in real terms.

Concerning the proposals for Bank of Japan reforms which were hammered out by a group of advisers to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and unveiled on Tuesday, Mitsuzuka said he had instructed a 15-member committee to study the proposals, which aim to strengthen the BOJ's independence.
